facts.statement: The genus was described based on specimen PVL-4035, which includes a coracoid, proximal scapula, and proximal humerus suspected to be the left shoulder of one individual.
facts.quote: It was described from specimen PVL-4035, a coracoid, proximal scapula and proximal humerus found close to each other and suspected to represent the left shoulder of a single individual.

facts.statement: The only currently accepted species, E. leali, comes from the Late Cretaceous Lecho Formation at El Brete, Argentina.
facts.quote: The type and only currently accepted species E. leali is from the Late Cretaceous Lecho Formation at El Brete, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus name means "opposite bird" because it possesses a reversed scapula-coracoid connection compared to modern birds and hesperornithids.
facts.quote: The genus and the larger group it belongs to, get their name from the reversed scapula-coracoid connection they possess compared to modern birds and the hesperornithids that were their contemporaries: Enanti "opposite", ornis is "bird".

facts.statement: Enantiornis leali is among the largest enantiornithines, reaching about 78.5 cm in length, 34 cm in hip height, 6.75 kg in weight, and a 1.2 m wingspan.
facts.quote: It is among the largest enantiornithines discovered to date, with a length in life of around 78.5 cm, hip height of 34 cm, weight of 6.75 kg, and wingspan comparable to herring gulls, around 1.2 m.

facts.statement: Enantiornis leali was placed in its own family, Enantiornithidae.
facts.quote: It was placed in a family of its own, Enantiornithidae.

facts.statement: Because no hindlimb elements are known, it is debated whether Enantiornis might include species like Lectavis, Soroavisaurus, or Yungavolucris known only from leg bones.
facts.quote: As no hindlimb elements are known from Enantiornis, it might include one of the El Brete enantiornithines known only from leg bones, namely Lectavis, Soroavisaurus or Yungavolucris.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Enantiornis leali is the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).
Enantiornis leali belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
The genus Enantiornis lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The ecological niche of Enantiornis leali resembled that of a mid-sized vulture or eagle.
rejected.quote: Its ecological niche resembled that of a mid-sized vulture or eagle.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'resembled that of a mid-sized vulture or eagle'
